pinyin: chāo yīng gǎn měi
literal: surpass · Britain · catch up with · America
natural: overtake Britain and catch up with America

meaning.en: A 1950s national goal of overtaking Britain and the United States in industrial output; also used for any ambitious catching-up target.
meaning.zh: 20世纪50年代末的国家目标，要在工业产量上超过英国、赶上美国；也泛指追赶先进的目标。

equivalents: catch up with and overtake the West

examples.zh: 大跃进时期提出了超英赶美的口号。
examples.en: The slogan of overtaking Britain and catching up with America was raised during the Great Leap Forward.

examples.zh: 公司立下超英赶美的目标，要追上国际大厂。
examples.en: The company set itself the goal of catching up with the international leaders.

usage.en: Linked to the 1957-58 aim of surpassing Britain in steel output within fifteen years. Often used with irony about over-ambitious goals. Neutral to formal.
usage.zh: 与1957至1958年提出的十五年内钢产量赶上英国的目标相联系。常带讽刺意味地指不切实际的目标。

pinyin: yǐ jiē jí dòu zhēng wéi gāng
literal: take · class · struggle · as · key link
natural: take class struggle as the key link

meaning.en: A political line of the 1960s-70s that made class struggle the central task of all work; formally abandoned in 1978.
meaning.zh: 20世纪六七十年代的政治路线，把阶级斗争当作一切工作的中心；1978年正式放弃。

equivalents: class struggle as the guiding line

examples.zh: 历史教科书讲到，党在1978年停止了以阶级斗争为纲。
examples.en: The textbook says the Party stopped taking class struggle as the key link in 1978.

examples.zh: 研究者分析了以阶级斗争为纲这一路线的影响。
examples.en: Researchers analysed the effects of the line of taking class struggle as the key link.

usage.en: A historical term used in discussing the Cultural Revolution and the 1978 shift to economic development. Formal, neutral.
usage.zh: 讨论文革及1978年转向经济建设时使用的历史术语。正式，中性。

pinyin: huà qīng jiè xiàn
literal: draw · clear · boundary · line
natural: draw a clear line

meaning.en: To separate oneself clearly from someone or something, especially to avoid being associated with it.
meaning.zh: 与某人或某事明确分开，不再牵连。

examples.zh: 他公开表示要与犯错的同事划清界限。
examples.en: He said publicly that he would draw a clear line between himself and his colleague who had erred.

examples.zh: 公司与违规行为划清界限。
examples.en: The company drew a clear line between itself and the misconduct.

usage.en: In the Cultural Revolution 'drawing a line' with a family member labelled a class enemy was demanded; today the phrase is general. Neutral.
usage.zh: 文革时期常要求与被定为阶级敌人的亲友“划清界限”；今天泛指明确切割。中性。

pinyin: zhī shi yuè duō yuè fǎn dòng
literal: knowledge · the more · the more · reactionary
natural: the more you know, the more reactionary you are

meaning.en: A Cultural Revolution-era slogan that treated educated people with suspicion; today quoted as an example of anti-intellectualism.
meaning.zh: 文革时期歧视知识分子的说法；今天作为反智主义的例子被引用。

examples.zh: 老教授回忆起知识越多越反动的年代，感慨万千。
examples.en: The old professor recalled the days of 'the more knowledge, the more reactionary' with deep feeling.

examples.zh: 知识越多越反动这种说法，如今已被彻底否定。
examples.en: The claim that the more knowledge you have, the more reactionary you are has long been rejected.

usage.en: Mainly cited historically, with disapproval, when talking about the treatment of intellectuals in 1966-76. Casual to neutral.
usage.zh: 主要在回顾1966至1976年知识分子的处境时作批评性引用。

pinyin: shàng shān xià xiāng
literal: go up · mountain · go down · countryside
natural: go up to the mountains and down to the countryside

meaning.en: The movement, mainly 1968-1978, in which millions of urban young people were sent to live and work in rural areas.
meaning.zh: 20世纪五十至七十年代（尤其是1968至1978年）数以千万计的城市青年到农村劳动和生活的运动。

equivalents: the Down to the Countryside Movement

examples.zh: 爷爷年轻时上山下乡，在农村待了八年。
examples.en: My grandfather went to the countryside in his youth and spent eight years there.

examples.zh: 上山下乡是一代人共同的记忆。
examples.en: The send-down movement is a shared memory of a generation.

origin.source: 1968年12月毛泽东号召知识青年到农村去

story.en: In December 1968 the People's Daily published Mao's instruction that educated youth should go to the countryside to be re-educated by the peasants, starting the mass movement.
story.zh: 1968年12月《人民日报》发表毛泽东的指示，要求知识青年到农村去接受再教育，运动由此大规模展开。

usage.en: The people involved are called 知青 (educated youth). Today also used in a lighter sense of going to rural areas, e.g. 干部上山下乡搞调研. Neutral.
usage.zh: 参与者称“知青”。今天也用于指到基层、农村做调研等。中性。

pinyin: guǎng kuò tiān dì, dà yǒu zuò wéi
literal: vast · open · world, greatly · have · achievement
natural: a vast stage on which one can achieve much

meaning.en: A broad field in which one can do great things; used of the countryside and, more widely, of any promising field.
meaning.zh: 天地广阔，可以大展身手。原指农村，也泛指前景广阔的领域。

examples.zh: 农业科技领域广阔天地，大有作为。
examples.en: In agricultural technology there is a vast stage on which much can be achieved.

examples.zh: 毕业生到西部去，那里广阔天地，大有作为。
examples.en: Graduates are heading west, where there is a vast stage for achievement.

origin.source: 毛泽东《中国农村的社会主义高潮》按语（1955年）

story.en: In 1955 Mao added an editor's note saying that the countryside is a vast stage in which one can achieve a great deal.
story.zh: 1955年毛泽东在编辑《中国农村的社会主义高潮》时写按语，称农村是一个广阔的天地，大有作为。

usage.en: Mao used it in 1955 about the countryside, and it became a slogan of the send-down movement. Today used positively about opportunity. Formal.
usage.zh: 1955年毛泽东在批语中以此指农村，后成为上山下乡运动的口号。今天多用于鼓励到基层、新领域发展。正式。

pinyin: xiàng léi fēng tóng zhì xué xí
literal: towards · Lei Feng · comrade · learn
natural: learn from Comrade Lei Feng

meaning.en: A slogan calling on people to follow the selfless, helpful spirit of soldier Lei Feng.
meaning.zh: 号召大家学习雷锋无私奉献、乐于助人的精神。

examples.zh: 每年三月，学校都组织向雷锋同志学习活动。
examples.en: Every March the school organises activities to learn from Comrade Lei Feng.

examples.zh: 社区的墙上挂着“向雷锋同志学习”的标语。
examples.en: A banner 'Learn from Comrade Lei Feng' hangs on the community wall.

story.en: On 5 March 1963 Mao Zedong wrote the inscription 'Learn from Comrade Lei Feng' (向雷锋同志学习), starting a nationwide campaign.
story.zh: 1963年3月5日，毛泽东为雷锋题词“向雷锋同志学习”，全国掀起学雷锋运动。

usage.en: March 5 is 'Learn from Lei Feng Day'. Today the slogan is widely used for volunteer activities. Formal, positive.
usage.zh: 3月5日为学雷锋纪念日。如今多用于志愿服务活动。正式，褒义。

pinyin: zuò hǎo shì bù liú míng
literal: do · good · deeds · not · leave · name
natural: do good deeds without leaving your name

meaning.en: To help others quietly, without seeking credit or thanks.
meaning.zh: 默默帮助别人，不求回报和名声。

examples.zh: 他经常捐款，却总是做好事不留名。
examples.en: He often donates but always does good without leaving his name.

examples.zh: 这位做好事不留名的老人，让大家很感动。
examples.en: The old man who does good deeds without leaving his name touched everyone.

usage.en: A phrase from the Lei Feng spirit; often seen in news about anonymous helpers. Neutral, positive.
usage.zh: 源于学雷锋精神，常见于匿名助人的新闻。中性偏褒。

text: 对待同志要像春天般温暖
pinyin: duì dài tóng zhì yào xiàng chūn tiān bān wēn nuǎn
literal: treat · comrades · should · like · spring · as · warm
natural: treat comrades with the warmth of spring

meaning.en: Treat colleagues and fellow members with kindness and warmth.
meaning.zh: 对待同事、同志要热情友好。

examples.zh: 班主任常说，对待同志要像春天般温暖。
examples.en: The head teacher often says to treat comrades with the warmth of spring.

examples.zh: 对待同志要像春天般温暖，团队气氛才好。
examples.en: Treat comrades like the warmth of spring and the team atmosphere will be good.

story.en: The line comes from the diary credited to the soldier Lei Feng, published after his death in 1962 and widely used in education.
story.zh: 出自传为雷锋所写的日记，1962年他去世后发表，广泛用于教育。

usage.en: The full line continues: work like summer fire, individualism like autumn wind, enemies like winter. Formal.
usage.zh: 原话后面接着：对待工作像夏天一样火热，对待个人主义像秋风扫落叶，对待敌人像严冬一样残酷。正式。

text: 有条件要上，没有条件创造条件也要上
pinyin: yǒu tiáo jiàn yào shàng, méi yǒu tiáo jiàn chuàng zào tiáo jiàn yě yào shàng
literal: have · conditions · must · go ahead, no · conditions · create · conditions · also · must · go ahead
natural: if conditions exist, go ahead; if not, create them and go ahead

meaning.en: Do not wait for ideal conditions; press on and create them yourself.
meaning.zh: 不等不靠，没有条件就创造条件去干。

examples.zh: 科研组缺设备，但有条件要上，没有条件创造条件也要上。
examples.en: The research team lacked equipment but pressed on and created the conditions.

examples.zh: 创业要有条件要上，没有条件创造条件也要上的精神。
examples.en: Starting up takes the spirit of creating the conditions you lack.

usage.en: Associated with the Daqing oilfield spirit of the 1960s and with 'iron man' Wang Jinxi. Formal, positive.
usage.zh: 与上世纪六十年代的大庆精神和“铁人”王进喜相联系。正式，褒义。

pinyin: tòu guò xiàn xiàng kàn běn zhì
literal: through · appearance · see · essence
natural: look through appearances to the essence

meaning.en: Do not stop at the surface of things; find the underlying cause or real nature.
meaning.zh: 不要停留在表面，要找到事物的根本原因或真实性质。

examples.zh: 分析数据时要透过现象看本质。
examples.en: When analysing data you must see the essence through the appearances.

examples.zh: 透过现象看本质，才能找到问题的根源。
examples.en: Only by looking through appearances to the essence can you find the root of the problem.

usage.en: A principle of Marxist philosophy, also very common in exam essays. Formal, positive.
usage.zh: 马克思主义哲学的基本方法，也是作文中的常用语。正式，褒义。

pinyin: sān dà jì lǜ bā xiàng zhù yì
literal: three · great · disciplines · eight · items · attention
natural: the Three Main Rules of Discipline and Eight Points for Attention

meaning.en: The code of conduct of the Chinese Red Army and PLA, including respect for the people and no taking of their property.
meaning.zh: 红军和人民解放军的行为准则，核心是尊重群众、不侵犯群众利益。

examples.zh: 新兵入伍第一课就是学习三大纪律八项注意。
examples.en: The first lesson for recruits is the Three Main Rules of Discipline and Eight Points for Attention.

examples.zh: 老兵常讲起三大纪律八项注意的故事。
examples.en: Veterans often tell stories about the Three Main Rules and Eight Points for Attention.

story.en: The final form of the rules was published in 1947 in the PLA's proclamation, building on those drawn up by Mao for the Red Army in 1928.
story.zh: 1947年的《中国人民解放军宣言》正式公布，沿袭了1928年毛泽东为红军制定的纪律。

usage.en: It began with 'three rules and six points' in 1928 and took its final form in 1947. Often quoted as a symbol of military discipline. Formal.
usage.zh: 1928年最初为“三大纪律六项注意”，1947年定型为三大纪律八项注意。常作为军纪的象征。正式。

pinyin: bù ná qún zhòng yī zhēn yī xiàn
literal: not · take · the masses' · one · needle · one · thread
natural: not take so much as a needle or thread from the people

meaning.en: To keep strictly honest and take nothing from ordinary people.
meaning.zh: 严守纪律，不占群众一点便宜。

equivalents: not take a pin from the people

examples.zh: 红军战士始终做到不拿群众一针一线。
examples.en: Red Army soldiers always kept to not taking a needle or thread from the people.

examples.zh: 廉政教育强调不拿群众一针一线。
examples.en: Anti-corruption education stresses not taking a needle or thread from the people.

story.en: The second of the Three Main Rules of Discipline of the Red Army, first drawn up in 1928; the second rule was originally worded 'don't take a single sweet potato from the people'.
story.zh: 红军三大纪律的第二条，1928年起制定；最初的说法是“不拿群众一个红薯”。

usage.en: The second of the Three Main Rules of Discipline; often quoted in anti-corruption writing. Formal.
usage.zh: 三大纪律中的第二条，常见于廉政宣传。正式。

pinyin: chéng qián bì hòu, zhì bìng jiù rén
literal: punish · past · be careful · future, cure · illness · save · person
natural: learn from past mistakes to avoid future ones, and cure the sickness to save the patient

meaning.en: Criticise errors so that people learn from them, with the aim of helping the person correct himself rather than destroying him.
meaning.zh: 批评错误是为了让人吸取教训、避免再犯，目的在于帮助人改正，而不是把人搞垮。

equivalents: correct the person, not destroy him

examples.zh: 处理这件事要惩前毖后，治病救人。
examples.en: In handling this case we should learn from the past and cure the person, not destroy him.

examples.zh: 领导对犯错的同事坚持惩前毖后，治病救人。
examples.en: The leader dealt with the colleague's mistake with the principle of curing the patient to save him.

origin.source: 毛泽东《整顿党的作风》（1942年）

story.en: In his February 1942 speech on rectifying Party style, Mao used 惩前毖后 (from the Shijing) and 治病救人 as the principle for dealing with comrades' errors.
story.zh: 1942年2月毛泽东在延安作《整顿党的作风》，提出对待错误要“惩前毖后，治病救人”。

usage.en: 惩前毖后 comes from the Shijing 《周颂·小毖》; Mao paired it with 治病救人 in 1942 as a principle for dealing with comrades' errors. Formal.
usage.zh: “惩前毖后”出自《诗经·周颂·小毖》；毛泽东1942年将其与“治病救人”并用，作为处理同志错误的方针。正式。

pinyin: qù cū qǔ jīng, qù wěi cún zhēn
literal: remove · coarse · take · refined, remove · false · keep · true
natural: discard the dross and keep the essence; discard the false and keep the true

meaning.en: In studying material, filter out what is crude or false and keep what is refined and true.
meaning.zh: 对材料要加以筛选，去掉粗劣虚假的，留下精华真实的。

equivalents: separate the wheat from the chaff

examples.zh: 研究资料时要去粗取精，去伪存真。
examples.en: When studying material we must discard the dross and keep the essence.

examples.zh: 网上信息太杂，要去粗取精，去伪存真。
examples.en: There is too much online information; discard the dross and the false.

story.en: In his 1937 essay On Practice, Mao described how the mind should process perceptual material: discard the dross, keep the essence, discard the false, keep the true, go from one to the other and from outside to inside.
story.zh: 1937年毛泽东在《实践论》中写道，对感性材料要去粗取精、去伪存真、由此及彼、由表及里。

usage.en: Often followed by 由此及彼，由表及里 in the same sentence. Formal, positive.
usage.zh: 常与“由此及彼，由表及里”连用。正式，褒义。

pinyin: shí gè zhǐ tou tán gāng qín
literal: ten · finger · play · piano
natural: play the piano with all ten fingers

meaning.en: To handle many tasks at once by putting them in order and giving each its proper weight, as a pianist uses all ten fingers.
meaning.zh: 同时处理多项工作时，要统筹兼顾，有轻有重，像弹钢琴一样十指协调。

examples.zh: 管理者要学会十个指头弹钢琴。
examples.en: A manager must learn to play the piano with all ten fingers.

examples.zh: 她同时负责三个项目，十个指头弹钢琴，一点不乱。
examples.en: She runs three projects at once, using all ten fingers like a pianist, and never gets confused.

origin.source: 毛泽东《党委会的工作方法》（1949年）

story.en: In this March 1949 note on working methods, Mao urged Party committee members to be able to 'play the piano' and coordinate several tasks at once.
story.zh: 1949年3月毛泽东在《党委会的工作方法》中要求党委成员学会“弹钢琴”，同时抓好多项工作。

usage.en: A management metaphor: the opposite is 'catching fleas with ten fingers' (十个指头捉跳蚤), which only gets confused. Casual to neutral.
usage.zh: 是个管理比喻，反面是“十个指头捉跳蚤”，一把抓只会乱。口语到中性。

pinyin: yī qiè xíng dòng tīng zhǐ huī
literal: all · action · listen · command
natural: all actions follow orders

meaning.en: Every action must follow the unified command; discipline is above personal choice.
meaning.zh: 一切行动都要服从统一指挥，保持严明纪律。

examples.zh: 队伍出发前，队长重申一切行动听指挥。
examples.en: Before setting out, the leader reminded everyone that all actions follow orders.

examples.zh: 救援现场一切行动听指挥，才能高效有序。
examples.en: At a rescue site all actions must follow command to be orderly and efficient.

story.en: The first of the Three Main Rules of Discipline of the Red Army, first drawn up in 1928; the rule was kept in the PLA's final form of 1947.
story.zh: 红军三大纪律的第一条，1928年起制定，1947年的定型版沿用。

usage.en: The first of the Three Main Rules of Discipline, and a common phrase in drills and team rules. Formal.
usage.zh: 三大纪律第一条，也是演练和团队规则中的常用语。正式。

pinyin: mō zhe shí tou guò hé
literal: feel · -ing · stones · cross · river
natural: cross the river by feeling for the stones

meaning.en: To advance step by step through trial and error when there is no ready-made path.
meaning.zh: 没有现成经验时，边试边改，稳步前进。

examples.zh: 改革初期，大家摸着石头过河。
examples.en: In the early days of reform, everyone crossed the river by feeling for the stones.

examples.zh: 新业务没有先例，只能摸着石头过河。
examples.en: With no precedent for the new business we can only feel our way.

usage.en: Associated with the economic reforms from 1978; often credited to Chen Yun and then promoted by Deng Xiaoping. Casual to neutral.
usage.zh: 与1978年后的经济改革相联系，一般认为是陈云提出，后经邓小平推广。口语到中性。

pinyin: fā zhǎn cái shì yìng dào lǐ
literal: development · only · is · hard · principle
natural: development is the only hard truth

meaning.en: Development is the key task, since it is what solves a country's many problems.
meaning.zh: 发展是解决各种问题的关键，是最重要的任务。

examples.zh: 改革开放的实践证明发展才是硬道理。
examples.en: The practice of reform and opening-up has shown that development is the hard truth.

examples.zh: 小城市也要抓住机会，发展才是硬道理。
examples.en: Small cities must also seize opportunities; development is what counts.

story.en: In his tour of southern China in early 1992, Deng Xiaoping said that development is the hard truth, pushing reform forward.
story.zh: 1992年初邓小平视察南方时讲话，提出“发展才是硬道理”，推动了改革开放。

usage.en: A key slogan of the reform era, widely used in government and business. Formal.
usage.zh: 改革开放时期的重要口号，政府和企业都常用。正式。

pinyin: liǎng shǒu zhuā, liǎng shǒu dōu yào yìng
literal: two · hands · grasp, two · hands · all · must · be · firm
natural: grasp with both hands, and make both firm

meaning.en: Pursue two tasks at once and give both equal firmness, neither slackening.
meaning.zh: 两项工作都要抓，而且两者都要抓紧、抓实。

equivalents: do both, and do both well

examples.zh: 环保与发展要两手抓，两手都要硬。
examples.en: Environmental protection and development must both be pursued firmly.

examples.zh: 校长强调成绩与品德两手抓，两手都要硬。
examples.en: The principal stressed grasping grades and character with both hands.

usage.en: A formula of the reform era, often quoted on material and cultural progress, and on construction and anti-corruption. Formal.
usage.zh: 改革开放时期的提法，常指物质文明与精神文明、建设与廉政等并重。正式。

pinyin: ràng yī bù fēn rén xiān fù qǐ lái
literal: let · one · part · people · first · get rich
natural: let some people get rich first

meaning.en: A reform-era principle of letting those who work hard and are able get rich first, so as to lead others to prosperity.
meaning.zh: 改革开放的政策：允许一部分人通过努力先富裕起来，再带动大家共同富裕。

examples.zh: 改革初期强调让一部分人先富起来。
examples.en: In the early reform years the emphasis was on letting some people get rich first.

examples.zh: 让一部分人先富起来，是为了最终共同富裕。
examples.en: Letting some people get rich first aims at common prosperity in the end.

usage.en: A key slogan of Deng Xiaoping's reforms, usually completed by 'to bring everyone along toward common prosperity'. In debate about inequality it is often discussed. Formal.
usage.zh: 邓小平改革思想的核心口号，后面常接“带动大家共同富裕”。在讨论贫富差距时常被提起。正式。

text: 科学技术是第一生产力
pinyin: kē xué jì shù shì dì yī shēng chǎn lì
literal: science · technology · is · first · productive force
natural: science and technology are the primary productive force

meaning.en: Science and technology are the main driver of economic growth.
meaning.zh: 科学技术是推动经济发展的首要动力。

equivalents: tech is the engine of growth

examples.zh: 科学技术是第一生产力，这家企业每年投入大量研发经费。
examples.en: Science and technology are the primary productive force, and this firm spends heavily on R&D each year.

examples.zh: 政府重申科学技术是第一生产力。
examples.en: The government repeated that science and technology are the primary productive force.

origin.source: 邓小平会见捷克斯洛伐克领导人时的谈话（1988年9月）

story.en: In September 1988 Deng Xiaoping, meeting the Czechoslovak Party leader Miloš Jakeš, said that science and technology are the primary productive force.
story.zh: 1988年9月邓小平会见捷克斯洛伐克领导人雅克什时说：“科学技术是第一生产力。”

usage.en: A core principle behind China's science and education policy. Formal, positive.
usage.zh: 中国科教政策的一项核心原则。正式，褒义。

pinyin: mǎ zhào pǎo, wǔ zhào tiào
literal: horses · as before · run, dancing · as before · dance
natural: the horses will still race and the dancing go on

meaning.en: Life will go on as usual; used of Hong Kong after 1997, to reassure that its way of life would not change.
meaning.zh: 一切照旧；用于回归后的香港，表示生活方式不变。

examples.zh: 回归后，香港仍是马照跑，舞照跳。
examples.en: After the return, Hong Kong still has its horses racing and its dancing.

examples.zh: 政策变了，但生活还是马照跑，舞照跳。
examples.en: Policy has changed but life goes on as usual.

usage.en: Associated with Deng Xiaoping in 1984, in the context of Hong Kong's future, often with 股照炒 (stocks still traded). Casual.
usage.zh: 与邓小平1984年谈香港前途相联系，常接“股照炒”。口语。
